notes:
Overview: fintech analytics provider. Heavy doc corpus (pricing models, contracts, transaction logs). Primary objective: accurate enterprise search with legal/compliance context + cheap reranking layer.

What they said: 'We need deterministic latency and clear cost math — can't have surprises during audits.'

Indexing & scale needs: currently estimate 50M-200M vectors (512d), growing ~30%/yr. Expect bursts of reindexing after nightly ETL. Need bulk S3 ingestion, incremental upserts, and low-latency namespace isolation per client segment.

Latency & throughput targets: P50 retrieval latency < 50-80ms for ANN search (top-100), P95 < 200ms end-to-end after reranking. Initial throughput target ~500-2,000 qps depending on product line. Rerank stage should add <50ms for lightweight cross-encoder on short contexts.

Cost sensitivity: finance team wants modeled cost/query < $0.002 at production throughput; willing to trade small latency increase for quantized indexes or caching. Looking for Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching + KV caching + quantized kernel suggestions).

Vector DB connector requirements (explicit asks):
- Support for HNSW + compressed indexes or IVF + PQ for 100M+ scale.
- Dot-product/cosine metric and consistent normalization across upsert/serving pipelines.
- Bulk ingest via S3 snapshots + streaming CDC from Postgres; idempotent upserts and tombstone support.
- Namespace/tenant isolation within same cluster, per-namespace RBAC.
- Upsert throughput: at least 10k vectors/sec for backfills.
- Index tuning hooks from Redwood Optimize (suggest quantization, efConstruction, efSearch settings).
- Strong metadata filtering (boolean + range) combined with ANN recall.
- Low-overhead TTL and lifecycle policies for short-lived vectors.
- Observability: per-query token/embedding cost breakdown + latency traces to correlate ANN vs rerank times.

Preferred vendors to test: Pinecone (managed, proven), Weaviate (policy + semantic filters), pgvector (cost-effective but needs sharding plan), Elastic (hybrid filter + ANN). They want a benchmark matrix from Redwood comparing throughput/latency/cost for each connector at 50M/100M/200M vectors.

Reranking architecture notes: prefer hybrid retrieval -> rerank pipeline: lightweight first-stage ANN (top-200) -> filter by metadata -> cross-encoder re-rank top-20. Wants Redwood to support server-side rerank hooks with fallback to cheaper local model if dedicated capacity saturated.

Security & compliance: data residency strict (EU for EU clients), KMS integration required for private deployments, audit logs retained 7 years for some regulated customers. SSO/SAML mandatory for admin console.

Open questions / asks from Pivot Vectra:
- Can Redwood provide a connector guarantee for pgvector at 100M+ scale?
- Example cost model for a 1k qps production workload (breakdown: ANN tier + rerank + tokens)?
- SLA for deterministic P95 latency under burst + fallback strategy when dedicated capacity is exceeded.

Next steps (short):
- 2025-03-03: POC kickoff meeting — ingest 50M vectors (S3 snapshot) + run cross-vendor benchmarks (Pinecone, pgvector, Weaviate). SE to deliver connector checklist.
- Legal: deliver data residency attestation (Redwood security FAQ link requested).
